title.en: The future: be going to (I am going to study)
title.es: El futuro: be going to (voy a hacer)

text.en: “Be going to” matches Spanish “ir a + infinitivo” almost exactly: “Voy a estudiar” = “I am going to study”. It expresses plans, intentions and predictions based on what we can see. The one big difference: instead of “ir” you need the right form of to be (am, is, are), and “a” becomes “to”, followed by the base verb.
text.es: «Be going to» equivale casi exactamente al «ir a + infinitivo» del español: «Voy a estudiar» = «I am going to study». Expresa planes, intenciones y predicciones basadas en lo que vemos. La única gran diferencia: en lugar de «ir» hace falta la forma correcta de to be (am, is, are), y la «a» se convierte en «to», seguida del verbo base.

rows: I am not going to study

text.en: Plans and intentions: something you have already decided. Clues: tomorrow, tonight, next week, soon.
text.es: Planes e intenciones: algo que ya has decidido. Pistas: tomorrow, tonight, next week, soon.

examples.es: We are going to visit Mexico next year.

tr.en: We are going to visit Mexico next year.
tr.es: Vamos a visitar México el año que viene.

text.en: Predictions when you can see the signs: Look at the clouds! It is going to rain.
text.es: Predicciones cuando ves las señales: Look at the clouds! It is going to rain.

examples.es: Look at the clouds! It is going to rain.

text.en: Negative: “not” after am / is / are (I’m not, isn’t, aren’t). Question: am / is / are moves to the front: Are you going to work?
text.es: Negación: «not» después de am / is / are (I’m not, isn’t, aren’t). Pregunta: am / is / are pasa al principio: Are you going to work?

examples.es: What are you going to do?

text.en: Am / is / are is required; you cannot drop it before “going to”. Do not say “I going to study” or “She going to work”; say “I am going to study”, “She is going to work”.
text.es: Am / is / are es obligatorio; no se puede omitir delante de «going to». No digas «I going to study» ni «She going to work», di «I am going to study», «She is going to work».

text.en: After “to” the base verb follows. Do not say “I am going to studying” or “She is going to works”; say “I am going to study”, “She is going to work”.
text.es: Después de «to» va el verbo base. No digas «I am going to studying» ni «She is going to works», di «I am going to study», «She is going to work».

text.en: Do not translate “ir” as “go” in the present tense. Do not say “I go to study tomorrow”; say “I am going to study tomorrow”.
text.es: No traduzcas «ir» como «go» en presente. No digas «I go to study tomorrow», di «I am going to study tomorrow».

text.en: With weather and predictions the subject “it” is required. Do not say “Is going to rain”; say “It is going to rain”.
text.es: Con el clima y las predicciones el sujeto «it» es obligatorio. No digas «Is going to rain», di «It is going to rain».

speak.en: The phrase «be going to» is the Spanish «ir a + infinitivo». It expresses plans and predictions: «I am going to study tonight», «She is going to visit her mother», «It is going to rain». «Am», «is» or «are» is required, followed by «to» and the base verb. Negative: «I am not going to work tomorrow». Questions: «Are you going to study?», «What are you going to do?». Careful: not «I going to study», and not «I go to study tomorrow».
speak.es: «Be going to» es el «ir a + infinitivo» del español. Expresa planes y predicciones: «I am going to study tonight», «She is going to visit her mother», «It is going to rain». «Am», «is» o «are» es obligatorio, seguido de «to» y el verbo base. Negación: «I am not going to work tomorrow». Pregunta: «Are you going to study?», «What are you going to do?». Cuidado: no «I going to study», y no «I go to study tomorrow».

why.en: With “I” you need “am”: I am going to study tonight.
why.es: Con «I» hace falta «am»: I am going to study tonight.

is.en: “Is” goes with he, she, it; with “I” you need “am”.
is.es: «Is» va con he, she, it; con «I» hace falta «am».

are.en: “Are” goes with you, we, they; with “I” you need “am”.
are.es: «Are» va con you, we, they; con «I» hace falta «am».

examples: I am going to cook tonight.
I am going to work tomorrow.

tr.en: I am going to study tonight.

items.sentence: She ___ going to visit her mother.

why.en: With “she” you need “is”: She is going to visit her mother.
why.es: Con «she» hace falta «is»: She is going to visit her mother.

are.en: “Are” goes with you, we, they; with “she” you need “is”.
are.es: «Are» va con you, we, they; con «she» hace falta «is».

am.en: “Am” goes only with “I”; with “she” you need “is”.
am.es: «Am» va solo con «I»; con «she» hace falta «is».

examples: He is going to call me.
My sister is going to travel.

tr.en: She is going to visit her mother.
tr.es: Ella va a visitar a su mamá.

items.sentence: They ___ going to travel next month.

why.en: With “they” you need “are”: They are going to travel next month.
why.es: Con «they» hace falta «are»: They are going to travel next month.

is.en: “Is” goes with he, she, it; with “they” you need “are”.
is.es: «Is» va con he, she, it; con «they» hace falta «are».

do.en: In “be going to” it is to be, not “do”: They are going to travel.
do.es: En «be going to» va to be, no «do»: They are going to travel.

examples: We are going to eat here.
You are going to like it.

tr.en: They are going to travel next month.
tr.es: Ellos van a viajar el próximo mes.

items.sentence: We are going ___ watch a movie.

why.en: After “going” comes “to” and the base verb: going to watch.
why.es: Después de «going» va «to» y el verbo base: going to watch.

for.en: “Going for” means something else; the plan structure is: going to + base verb.
for.es: «Going for» significa otra cosa; la estructura del plan es: going to + verbo base.

at.en: “At” does not fit here; the structure is: going to + base verb.
at.es: «At» no encaja aquí; la estructura es: going to + verbo base.

examples: We are going to eat now.
They are going to play.

tr.en: We are going to watch a movie.
I am going to study.

text.en: plan, intention: be going to + base verb
text.es: plan, intención: be going to + verbo base

text.en: movement to a place: I am going to school
text.es: movimiento a un lugar: I am going to school

wrong.en: After “to” comes a verb (study), not a place, so this is a plan, not movement.
wrong.es: Después de «to» va un verbo (study), no un lugar, así que es un plan, no un movimiento.

text.en: present continuous: I am studying right now
text.es: presente continuo: estoy estudiando ahora mismo

wrong.en: “Going to” + base verb marks a future plan; an action in progress would take -ing (studying).
wrong.es: «Going to» + verbo base marca un plan futuro; una acción en curso llevaría -ing (studying).

why.en: After “to” the verb stays in its base form: I’m going to work tomorrow.
why.es: Después de «to» el verbo va en forma base: I’m going to work tomorrow.

working.en: There is no -ing after “going to”: going to work.
working.es: Después de «going to» no hay -ing: going to work.

works.en: After “going to” the verb takes no -s: going to work.
works.es: Después de «going to» el verbo no lleva -s: going to work.

examples: He's going to work tomorrow.
We are going to work.

tr.en: I'm going to work tomorrow.

items.sentence: He is going to ___ a cake.

why.en: After “to” the verb stays in its base form: He is going to make a cake.
why.es: Después de «to» el verbo va en forma base: He is going to make a cake.

makes.en: After “going to” the verb takes no -s, not even with “he”: make.
makes.es: Después de «going to» el verbo no lleva -s, ni siquiera con «he»: make.

making.en: There is no -ing after “going to”: going to make.
making.es: Después de «going to» no hay -ing: going to make.

examples: She is going to make dinner.
I am going to make a party.

tr.en: He is going to make a cake.
tr.es: Él va a hacer un pastel.

items.sentence: I ___ going to work tomorrow. It is Sunday.

why.en: The negative is: am not + going to: I am not going to work tomorrow.
why.es: La negación es: am not + going to: I am not going to work tomorrow.

don't.en: The negative of “be going to” uses to be, not “don’t”: I am not going to.
don't.es: La negación de «be going to» usa to be, no «don’t»: I am not going to.

no.en: “No” copies the Spanish pattern; English needs “am not”: I am not going to.
no.es: «No» copia el patrón del español; el inglés necesita «am not»: I am not going to.

examples: I am not going to eat here.
I am not going to call.

tr.en: I am not going to work tomorrow. It is Sunday.
tr.es: No voy a trabajar mañana. Es domingo.

items.sentence: She ___ going to eat here. She is not hungry.

why.en: With “she” you need “isn’t”: She isn’t going to eat here.
why.es: Con «she» hace falta «isn’t»: She isn’t going to eat here.

aren't.en: “Aren’t” goes with you, we, they; with “she” you need “isn’t”.
aren't.es: «Aren’t» va con you, we, they; con «she» hace falta «isn’t».

doesn't.en: The negative of “be going to” uses to be, not “doesn’t”.
doesn't.es: La negación de «be going to» usa to be, no «doesn’t».

examples: He isn't going to work.
It isn't going to rain.

tr.en: She isn't going to eat here. She is not hungry.
tr.es: Ella no va a comer aquí. No tiene hambre.

why.en: In the question “are” moves to the front: Are you going to study tonight?
why.es: En la pregunta «are» pasa al principio: Are you going to study tonight?

Do.en: In a “be going to” question to be comes first, not “do”: Are you going to…?
Do.es: En una pregunta con «be going to» va primero to be, no «do»: Are you going to…?

Is.en: “Is” goes with he, she, it; with “you” you need “Are”.
Is.es: «Is» va con he, she, it; con «you» hace falta «Are».

examples: Are they going to work?
Is she going to call?

tr.en: Are you going to study tonight?
She isn't going to eat.

text.en: negative: the negative of to be before going to
text.es: negación: la negación de to be antes de going to

wrong.en: The helper of “be going to” is to be, so “isn’t”, not “doesn’t”.
wrong.es: El auxiliar de «be going to» es to be, por eso «isn’t», no «doesn’t».

text.en: negative after going: going not to
text.es: negación después de going: going not to

wrong.en: “Not” comes after am / is / are, not after “going”: isn’t going to.
wrong.es: «Not» va después de am / is / are, no después de «going»: isn’t going to.

why.en: After the question word comes to be: What are you going to do?
why.es: Después de la palabra interrogativa va to be: What are you going to do?

do.en: Before “going to” comes to be, not “do”: What are you going to do?
do.es: Antes de «going to» va to be, no «do»: What are you going to do?

is.en: “Is” goes with he, she, it; with “you” you need “are”.
is.es: «Is» va con he, she, it; con «you» hace falta «are».

examples: What is she going to eat?
What are they going to do?

tr.en: What are you going to do?

why.en: With “they” you need “are”: Where are they going to live?
why.es: Con «they» hace falta «are»: Where are they going to live?

do.en: In a “be going to” question it is to be, not “do”: Where are they going to…?
do.es: En una pregunta con «be going to» va to be, no «do»: Where are they going to…?

does.en: “Does” does not fit “they”, and the structure uses to be: are.
does.es: «Does» no encaja con «they», y la estructura usa to be: are.

examples: Where are you going to work?
Where is he going to eat?

tr.en: Where are they going to live?

items.sentence: Look at the clouds! It ___ going to rain.

why.en: With “it” you need “is”, and the clouds are a sign for the prediction: It is going to rain.
why.es: Con «it» hace falta «is», y las nubes son la señal de la predicción: It is going to rain.

are.en: “Are” goes with you, we, they; with “it” you need “is”.
are.es: «Are» va con you, we, they; con «it» hace falta «is».

does.en: In “be going to” it is to be, not “does”: It is going to rain.
does.es: En «be going to» va to be, no «does»: It is going to rain.

examples: It is going to be hot.
The baby is going to sleep.

tr.en: Look at the clouds! It is going to rain.

items.es: Look! It is going to rain.

tr.en: Look! It is going to rain.

text.en: a prediction from signs we can see now
text.es: una predicción a partir de señales que vemos ahora

wrong.en: Rain is not a timetable: “Look!” shows that we are concluding from signs.
wrong.es: La lluvia no es un horario: «Look!» muestra que deducimos a partir de señales.

text.es: un hábito que se repite a menudo

wrong.en: This is a specific, near event, not a habit; a habit needs the present simple.
wrong.es: Es un hecho concreto y cercano, no un hábito; un hábito necesita el presente simple.

items.sentence: She is going to call me ___.

why.en: A plan for the future needs a future time expression: tomorrow.
why.es: Un plan para el futuro pide una expresión de tiempo futuro: tomorrow.

yesterday.en: “Yesterday” is past; “going to” points to the future: tomorrow.
yesterday.es: «Yesterday» es pasado; «going to» apunta al futuro: tomorrow.

last week.en: “Last week” is past; “going to” points to the future: tomorrow.
last week.es: «Last week» es pasado; «going to» apunta al futuro: tomorrow.

examples: We are going to eat tonight.
He is going to work soon.

tr.en: She is going to call me tomorrow.
tr.es: Ella me va a llamar mañana.

items.sentence: They are going to arrive ___ week.

why.en: For the future we say “next week”: They are going to arrive next week.
why.es: Para el futuro decimos «next week»: They are going to arrive next week.

last.en: “Last week” is past; “going to” points to the future: next week.
last.es: «Last week» es pasado; «going to» apunta al futuro: next week.

ago.en: “Ago” marks past time and follows a number (a week ago); for the future you need “next week”.
ago.es: «Ago» marca tiempo pasado y va después de un número (a week ago); para el futuro hace falta «next week».

examples: We are going to visit next month.
She is going to call next week.

tr.en: They are going to arrive next week.
tr.es: Ellos van a llegar la próxima semana.
